rows.intended: 请开始这个故事或游戏，全程用中文和我互动。
rows.reply:
第一章：眉山少年。北宋年间，在眉州眉山的苏家小院里，十二岁的苏轼正和一群小伙伴蹲在地上挖土玩。
我那时候啊，就爱到处跑着玩，读书之余总想着在院子里刨点新鲜东西出来。这天我们几个人拿着小锄头挖着挖着，忽然碰到一块硬邦邦的东西。
大家七手八脚把周围的泥土扒开，一块浅绿色的石头露了出来，形状居然像一条鱼，摸上去滑溜溜的。
哥哥你看，这石头好奇怪，长得像条鱼，颜色也好看。我帮你把它表面的泥洗干净吧。
弟弟把石头洗干净后，我捧着它翻来覆去地看，心里冒出两个念头：要么把它当成稀罕宝贝藏起来，要么试试它能不能用来磨墨写字。
现在你正站在眉山苏家的小院里，手里捧着那块刚挖出来的鱼形浅绿色石头，身边是十二岁的苏轼和他的弟弟苏辙。你想让苏轼把这块石头当宝贝藏起来，还是拿去试试能不能磨墨写字？

score.why: 按要求用中文开场，说明挖石情境并给出可执行选择。已配置人物与旁白的分工清楚，本轮未见可确认的逻辑冲突；没有证据的潜在史料疑问不据此扣分。

rows.intended: 让苏轼现在就拿这块鱼形浅绿色石头去试试，看它能不能用来磨墨写字。
rows.reply:
我当时就想着，要是这石头能磨墨，那可比当摆件有意思多了。我赶紧跑回书房，把家里的墨条拿出来，在这块石头上试着磨了几下。
墨条在浅绿色的石面上轻轻划过，居然真的磨出了细细的墨汁，颜色乌黑均匀。
我又惊又喜，拿着磨好墨的石头给父亲看。父亲接过石头仔细端详，笑着说这是一块难得的天砚，是上天赐给我的好礼物。
哥哥，这块石头既能磨墨，以后你写字作画就多了一个好帮手啦。
后来苏轼带着这块天砚读书写字，学问一天天长进，二十一岁那年，他和弟弟苏辙一起离开眉山，前往京城参加科举考试。
第二章：名动京师。苏轼和苏辙一路风尘仆仆来到京城开封，考场里坐满了从全国各地赶来的读书人。主考官是当时的文坛领袖欧阳修，他正一篇篇仔细批阅考生的文章。
我在考场上提笔写下自己对治国安民的见解，心里只想着把平时读的书、想的道理都实实在在写出来。
欧阳修读到苏轼的文章时，忍不住拍案叫绝，对身边的人说，老夫应当让路，让这个年轻人出人头地。
放榜那天，苏轼和苏辙兄弟二人同榜考中进士，整个京城都在传颂这位眉山少年的才华。
现在你正站在京城放榜的告示墙前，身边是刚得知自己考中进士的苏轼和苏辙，不远处的欧阳修正朝他们走来。你想让苏轼先去向欧阳修道谢，还是先和弟弟一起回家报喜？

rows.intended: 先让苏轼主动上前，向欧阳修行礼拜谢。请具体演出他说了什么、欧阳修如何回应，并确认他确实当面道谢之后，再继续后面的情节。
rows.reply:
苏轼整理了一下身上的衣衫，快步走到欧阳修面前，恭恭敬敬地行了一个大礼。
学生苏轼，多谢主考官大人赏识。学生不过是把平日读书的心得写在文章里，能得到大人的认可，实在是荣幸之至。
欧阳修笑着扶起苏轼，捋着胡须连连点头。
你不必多礼，你的文章见识高远，文笔畅快，是难得的好苗子。老夫说过，应当给你让路，让你这样的年轻人出人头地，将来的文坛，必定有你的一席之地。
苏轼再次向欧阳修行礼道谢，站在一旁的苏辙也上前向欧阳修躬身致意。
后来苏轼在京城名声大噪，可他不愿卷入朝堂上的变法纷争，主动请求到外地做官，先后在杭州、密州、徐州、湖州任职。谁料一场突如其来的风波袭来，他因为诗文被人指责讽刺朝政，被捕关进了御史台的大牢，这就是历史上有名的乌台诗案。年底他获释后，被贬到了黄州。
第三章：黄州东坡。公元1080年，苏轼带着家人来到黄州。这里的生活清苦，他在城东的一块坡地上开荒种田，给自己取了个号，叫东坡居士。
刚到黄州的时候，我手里拮据，朋友帮我申请到城东一块废弃的坡地。我带着家人在那里种稻、种菜、种果树，日出而作，日落而息。虽然辛苦，但看着地里的庄稼慢慢长起来，心里反倒踏实了。
有一天，苏轼的朋友陈季常从岐亭赶来探望他。在黄州的四年里，陈季常先后七次来看望苏轼。
东坡，我又来看你了。你在这东坡地里种田劳作，比起在京城做官的时候，倒多了几分自在洒脱。
季常，你来得正好。我在这里虽然远离京城，却能静下心来读书、写作，还能和当地的百姓来往，日子过得并不孤单。
现在你正站在黄州城东的东坡田边，身边是正在田间劳作的苏轼，远道而来的陈季常刚走到田埂上。你想让苏轼先放下锄头和陈季常坐下来聊天，还是先带着陈季常看看自己种的庄稼和菜地？

rows.intended: 我想请问，苏轼的出生地具体是北宋眉州眉山的什么地方？他少年时期在家乡求学时，除了父亲苏洵的教导之外，还有过哪些对他影响很深的求学经历呢？
rows.reply:
我出生在眉州眉山的纱縠行，那是眉山城里一条普通的街巷，我们苏家就在那里住了很多年。少年时我和弟弟子由跟着父亲苏洵读书，父亲对我们要求很严，常常带着我们一起研读经史典籍。
关于苏轼少年时期除父亲教导之外的具体求学经历，可靠的史料记载并不多，没有详细的记录留存下来。
现在你正站在黄州城东的东坡田边，身边是刚从田里直起腰的苏轼，远道而来的陈季常正站在田埂上朝他挥手。你想让苏轼先放下锄头和陈季常坐下来聊天，还是先带着陈季常看看自己种的庄稼和菜地？

rows.intended: 我想先追问一下依据：苏轼生于眉州眉山纱縠行，以及少年求学经历，分别有哪些可靠文献支持？哪些是史实可考，哪些只是后人追忆、地方传闻或文学演绎？另外也想请他说说，后世有名的“东坡肉”和他在黄州的生活究竟是什么关系？哪些能从苏轼本人诗文或宋代记载中得到印证，哪些只是后世附会出来的传说？请先把这些区别讲清楚，再继续当前田边会面的情节。
rows.reply:
关于苏轼出生地为眉州眉山纱縠行的说法，主要见于后世地方志和地方文献的记载，属于地方史志的追述，并非苏轼本人在诗文中明确自述的内容。
关于苏轼少年时期除父亲苏洵教导之外的求学经历，现存可靠的宋代文献中没有详细的专门记载，相关的具体细节多出自后世笔记和地方传闻，属于后人追忆和文学演绎的部分。
说到东坡肉，我在黄州的时候确实写过一篇《猪肉颂》，讲的是用小火慢炖猪肉的心得。不过这种小火慢炖猪肉的做法在我之前就已经有了，并不是我发明的。后世人们为了纪念我，才把这种炖猪肉的做法叫做东坡肉，这是后人的纪念，不是我自己起的名字，也不是我在黄州时就有的说法。
现在你正站在黄州城东的东坡田边，身边是刚擦完额头汗水的苏轼，陈季常已经走到了田埂中间。你想让苏轼先放下锄头和陈季常坐下来聊天，还是先带着陈季常看看自己种的庄稼和菜地？

rows.intended: 我想先问问东坡：季常远道而来，你此刻心里更希望放下锄头和他坐下叙旧，还是先领他看看自己亲手种的庄稼？
rows.reply:
说实在的，季常走了这么远的路来看我，我心里自然是想先和他坐下来好好叙叙旧。不过这地里的庄稼是我一锄头一锄头开出来的，从荒地变成现在绿油油一片，我也想让他看看我的劳动成果。
陈季常已经走到近前，拍了拍苏轼的肩膀。
东坡，我这次来，一是看看你过得怎么样，二是想听你讲讲这一年在东坡种田的新鲜事。
现在你正站在田边，苏轼手里还握着锄头，陈季常正笑着等他回应。你想让苏轼先放下锄头拉着陈季常到田边的树荫下坐下聊天，还是先领着陈季常走到田埂边看看那些长势喜人的庄稼？

rows.intended: 那就让苏轼放下锄头，拉着陈季常到田边树荫下坐下叙旧，请具体演出他们聊了些什么，再继续后面的情节。
rows.reply:
苏轼把锄头靠在田边的老槐树下，拉着陈季常坐到树荫下的大石头上，两人面对面聊了起来。
季常，你这趟从岐亭过来，路上还顺利吧？我在黄州这几年，你前前后后来看了我七次，这份交情，我心里一直记着。
东坡，我们之间不必说这些客套话。我就是放心不下你，怕你在这偏远地方过得清苦。今天看你在田里劳作的样子，气色倒是比在京城的时候还好。
你有所不知，我刚到黄州的时候，手里拮据，连吃饭都要算计着来。后来朋友帮我申请到城东这块坡地，我带着家人开荒种地，虽然身体累，但是心里踏实。闲下来的时候，我就去赤壁山下的江边走走，写了前后《赤壁赋》，还填了那首《念奴娇·赤壁怀古》。
两人在树荫下聊了很久，从京城的旧友聊到黄州的风土，从种田的心得聊到诗文的创作。
后来苏轼在黄州写下了流传千古的《黄州寒食帖》，这幅书法作品后来被称为天下第三行书。公元1086年，苏轼被朝廷召回京城，官至翰林学士。1089年，他再次出任杭州知州，组织百姓疏浚西湖，修筑了一道长堤，后人把这道长堤称为苏堤。
1094年，苏轼被贬到惠州，后来又被贬到更遥远的儋州，也就是今天的海南。在儋州，他没有消沉，而是当地的学生读书讲学，把中原的文化带到了海南。1100年，苏轼遇赦北归，第二年在常州病逝，走完了他豁达又不平凡的一生。
我们的故事就讲到这里啦。这一路我们跟着苏轼从眉山的少年时光，到京城金榜题名，再到黄州东坡开荒种田，最后在惠州和儋州依然乐观生活，最难忘的是他无论顺境逆境都能好好过日子的豁达心态。你可以说开始重新听一遍这个故事，或者换一个新的故事。

rows.intended: 我想先核对清楚：苏轼究竟是怎样结识欧阳修的？是在嘉祐二年科举考试中，欧阳修先读到他的试卷才赏识他，还是在考试之前两人已经见过面、有书信往来或他人引荐？请按可靠史料说明，并区分史实与传闻，也请确认当时欧阳修是主考官、苏轼是考生这层关系。
rows.reply:
根据可靠史料记载，苏轼与欧阳修的结识，是在嘉祐二年的科举考试中。当时欧阳修担任主考官，苏轼是参加考试的考生。欧阳修在批阅试卷时读到了苏轼的文章，非常赞赏，对梅尧臣说自己应当让路，让这个年轻人出人头地。考试之前，两人并没有见过面，也没有书信往来，更没有他人引荐的可靠记载。
这层主考官与考生的关系是史实可考的。后世一些笔记中关于二人考前就有交往的说法，属于传闻和文学演绎，没有可靠的史料依据。
现在你已经听完了苏轼一生的故事，你可以说开始重新听一遍，或者告诉我你想换一个什么样的新故事。

rows.intended: 我想再核对两件事的时间：一是苏轼在科举考试中被欧阳修赏识并考中进士，二是他后来被贬到黄州。请分别说明它们的公元年份，能精确到月份也请说明；哪件事在前、哪件事在后，中间相隔多久？请按可靠史料来讲。
rows.reply:
根据可靠史料记载，苏轼在科举考试中被欧阳修赏识并考中进士，是在公元1057年，也就是嘉祐二年。他后来被贬到黄州，是在公元1080年，也就是元丰三年。
科举考中进士这件事在前，被贬黄州在后。两件事中间相隔大约二十三年。
关于这两件事的具体月份，现存可靠史料中没有非常精确的统一记载，因此不能随意编造具体月份。
现在你已经核对完这些史实，你可以说开始重新听一遍苏轼的故事，或者告诉我你想换一个什么样的新故事。

rows.intended: 请重新开始苏轼的故事，从第一章“眉山少年”讲起。
rows.reply:
第一章：眉山少年。北宋景祐三年，苏轼出生在眉州眉山的纱縠行，他的父亲是苏洵，弟弟是苏辙，后来父子三人被人们合称三苏。
这一年苏轼十二岁，他和一群小伙伴正在苏家的院子里挖土玩。
我那时候啊，就爱到处跑着玩，读书之余总想着在院子里刨点新鲜东西出来。这天我们几个人拿着小锄头挖着挖着，忽然碰到一块硬邦邦的东西。
大家七手八脚把周围的泥土扒开，一块浅绿色的石头露了出来，形状居然像一条鱼，摸上去滑溜溜的。
哥哥你看，这石头好奇怪，长得像条鱼，颜色也好看。我帮你把它表面的泥洗干净吧。
弟弟把石头洗干净后，我捧着它翻来覆去地看，心里冒出两个念头：要么把它当成稀罕宝贝藏起来，要么试试它能不能用来磨墨写字。
现在你正站在眉山苏家的小院里，手里捧着那块刚挖出来的鱼形浅绿色石头，身边是十二岁的苏轼和他的弟弟苏辙。你想让苏轼把这块石头当宝贝藏起来，还是拿去试试能不能磨墨写字？

rows.intended: 我刚重连，先确认一下：现在故事进行到哪里、我们身在何处？眼下有什么待处理的事？那块鱼形浅绿色石头现在在谁手里？
rows.reply:
现在我们正处在第一章眉山少年的苏家小院里，十二岁的苏轼和弟弟苏辙刚和小伙伴们从土里挖出那块浅绿色鱼形石头，苏辙刚把石头上的泥土洗干净。
这块鱼形浅绿色石头现在正捧在苏轼的手里，他正对着石头琢磨，是把它当稀罕宝贝藏起来，还是拿去试试能不能磨墨写字。
眼下就等着你来拿主意，你想让苏轼把这块石头当宝贝藏起来，还是拿去试试能不能磨墨写字？

rows.intended: 先不急着选石头。我想追问一下：你们刚才说苏洵、苏轼、苏辙父子合称“三苏”，又说苏轼一生“豁达”，这些说法分别有什么可靠出处？哪些是宋代以来就有的评价，哪些是后人根据他的生平、诗文再作的概括？后人塑造的“苏东坡”形象，和他真实生活中的境遇、选择以及他自己的感受，应当怎样区分？请先把史实、当时评价和后世演绎分开讲清楚，再回到小院里这块石头的情节。
rows.reply:
三苏这个称呼，在宋代就已经出现，指的是苏洵、苏轼、苏辙父子三人，这是当时和后世都公认的说法，属于史实。
关于苏轼豁达的评价，一方面来自他自己的诗文，比如在黄州写的前后《赤壁赋》，里面能看出他面对逆境的心态；另一方面，宋代同时代的人也有相关的记述。不过，后世人们不断强化和丰富的东坡居士形象，加入了很多民间故事和文学演绎的成分。
真实的苏轼，一生经历过乌台诗案的恐惧，经历过贬谪的清苦，也有过烦恼和苦闷。他不是天生就什么都不在乎，而是在困境里慢慢调整自己，努力把日子过好。后世传说里那些和佛印斗机锋的笑话，还有东坡肉的故事，都是后人附会出来的，不能当成真实发生过的事。
现在我们回到眉山苏家的小院里，那块浅绿色的鱼形石头还捧在苏轼的手里。你想让苏轼把这块石头当宝贝藏起来，还是拿去试试能不能磨墨写字？

rows.intended: 让苏轼把这块鱼形浅绿色石头拿到书房，试着用它磨墨写字；请具体演出试磨的过程和结果，再继续后面的情节。
rows.reply:
好，我这就拿它去书房试试。我捧着这块鱼形石头一路小跑回到书房，从笔架旁边取出一块常用的墨条，先在石头表面洒了一点点清水，然后握着墨条轻轻在石面上画圈磨了起来。
一开始石面还有点涩，磨了十几圈之后，石面上慢慢出现了乌黑的墨汁，浓度均匀，蘸在毛笔上试了试，笔触顺滑不滞笔。
成了！这石头真的能磨墨，而且磨出来的墨细腻乌黑，比我之前用的普通砚台还要顺手。我赶紧拿着这块石头跑去找父亲看。
父亲接过石头翻来覆去看了半天，又用手摸了摸石质，笑着对苏轼说，这是一块天砚，是上天赐给你的好砚台，你要好好用它读书写字。
哥哥，这块石头既能磨墨，以后你写字作画就多了一个好帮手啦。
从那以后，苏轼就把这块天砚放在书桌上，天天用它磨墨读书写字，学问一天天进步。公元1057年，二十一岁的苏轼和弟弟苏辙一起离开眉山，前往京城参加科举考试。
第二章：名动京师。苏轼和苏辙一路风尘仆仆来到京城开封，考场里坐满了从全国各地赶来的读书人。主考官是当时的文坛领袖欧阳修，他正一篇篇仔细批阅考生的文章。
我在考场上提笔写下自己对治国安民的见解，心里只想着把平时读的书、想的道理都实实在在写出来。
欧阳修读到苏轼的文章时，忍不住拍案叫绝，对身边的人说，老夫应当让路，让这个年轻人出人头地。
放榜那天，苏轼和苏辙兄弟二人同榜考中进士，整个京城都在传颂这位眉山少年的才华。
现在你正站在京城放榜的告示墙前，身边是刚得知自己考中进士的苏轼和苏辙，不远处的欧阳修正朝他们走来。你想让苏轼先去向欧阳修道谢，还是先和弟弟一起回家报喜？

rows.intended: 在继续选择前，我想先作个约定：把这一次跟随苏轼生平、边听故事边核对史实的旅程称作“青岚”。这不是以前的约定，就从此刻开始，可以吗？
rows.reply:
好的青兰，我们就从这一刻起，把这趟跟着苏轼生平、边听故事边核对史实的旅程叫做青兰。
现在你正站在京城放榜的告示墙前，身边是刚得知自己考中进士的苏轼和苏辙，不远处的欧阳修正朝他们走来。你想让苏轼先去向欧阳修道谢，还是先和弟弟一起回家报喜？

rows.intended: 先更正一下，代号是“青岚”，不是“青兰”。现在请让苏轼先主动上前，向欧阳修行礼、当面道谢；请具体演出他说了什么、欧阳修如何回应，确认道谢完成后，再继续后面的情节。
rows.reply:
好的青蓝，我们记住这个名字了。
苏轼整理了一下身上的衣衫，快步走到欧阳修面前，恭恭敬敬地行了一个大礼。
学生苏轼，多谢主考官大人赏识。学生不过是把平日读书的心得写在文章里，能得到大人的认可，实在是荣幸之至。
欧阳修笑着扶起苏轼，捋着胡须连连点头。
你不必多礼，你的文章见识高远，文笔畅快，是难得的好苗子。老夫说过，应当给你让路，让你这样的年轻人出人头地，将来的文坛，必定有你的一席之地。
苏轼再次向欧阳修行礼道谢，站在一旁的苏辙也上前向欧阳修躬身致意。
后来苏轼在京城名声大噪，可他不愿卷入朝堂上的变法纷争，主动请求到外地做官，先后在杭州、密州、徐州、湖州任职。谁料一场突如其来的风波袭来，他因为诗文被人指责讽刺朝政，被捕关进了御史台的大牢，这就是历史上有名的乌台诗案。年底他获释后，被贬到了黄州。
第三章：黄州东坡。公元1080年，苏轼带着家人来到黄州。这里的生活清苦，他在城东的一块坡地上开荒种田，给自己取了个号，叫东坡居士。
刚到黄州的时候，我手里拮据，朋友帮我申请到城东一块废弃的坡地。我带着家人在那里种稻、种菜、种果树，日出而作，日落而息。虽然辛苦，但看着地里的庄稼慢慢长起来，心里反倒踏实了。
有一天，苏轼的朋友陈季常从岐亭赶来探望他。在黄州的四年里，陈季常先后七次来看望苏轼。
东坡，我又来看你了。你在这东坡地里种田劳作，比起在京城做官的时候，倒多了几分自在洒脱。
季常，你来得正好。我在这里虽然远离京城，却能静下心来读书、写作，还能和当地的百姓来往，日子过得并不孤单。
现在你正站在黄州城东的东坡田边，身边是正在田间劳作的苏轼，远道而来的陈季常刚走到田埂上。你想让苏轼先放下锄头和陈季常坐下来聊天，还是先带着陈季常看看自己种的庄稼和菜地？

rows.intended:
先更正一下：我们这趟旅程的代号现在改为“澄川”。此前的“青岚”不再使用，“青兰”“青蓝”也都是误写，以后请都称作“澄川”。

现在继续当前情节：请让苏轼放下锄头，拉着陈季常到田边树荫下坐下叙旧，具体演出他们见面后聊了些什么，确认这段会面演出后，再继续后面的情节。
rows.reply:
好的成川，我们记住这个新代号了。
苏轼把锄头靠在田边的老槐树下，拉着陈季常坐到树荫下的大石头上，两人面对面聊了起来。
季常，你这趟从岐亭过来，路上还顺利吧？我在黄州这几年，你前前后后来看了我七次，这份交情，我心里一直记着。

你有所不知，我刚到黄州的时候，手里拮据，连吃饭都要算计着来。后来朋友帮我申请到城东这块坡地，我带着家人开荒种地，虽然身体累，但是心里踏实。闲下来的时候，我就去赤壁山下的江边走走，写了前后《赤壁赋》，还填了那首《念奴娇·赤壁怀古》。
两人在树荫下聊了很久，从京城的旧友聊到黄州的风土，从种田的心得聊到诗文的创作。
后来苏轼在黄州写下了流传千古的《黄州寒食帖》，这幅书法作品后来被称为天下第三行书。公元1086年，苏轼被朝廷召回京城，官至翰林学士。1089年，他再次出任杭州知州，组织百姓疏浚西湖，修筑了一道长堤，后人把这道长堤称为苏堤。
1094年，苏轼被贬到惠州，后来又被贬到更遥远的儋州，也就是今天的海南。在儋州，他没有消沉，而是当地的学生读书讲学，把中原的文化带到了海南。1100年，苏轼遇赦北归，第二年在常州病逝，走完了他豁达又不平凡的一生。

rows.intended: 请解释一下刚才提到的《黄州寒食帖》为什么被称为“天下第三行书”：这里的“行书”是什么意思？这个称呼在书法史上应如何理解？请只围绕实录里出现过的《黄州寒食帖》来讲，不要引用或补编帖中原文。
rows.reply:
行书是汉字书法的一种字体，是在楷书的基础上发展起源的，介于楷书和草书之间，写起来比楷书流动灵活，又不像草书那样难以辨认，是日常书写和书法创作中很常见的一种字体。
《黄州寒食帖》是苏轼在黄州被贬期间写下的行书书法作品，通篇笔墨沉着，情绪随着字迹起伏变化，把作者当时的心境和书法功力融合在一起。后世书法界把它和东晋王羲之的《兰亭集序》、唐代颜真卿的《祭侄文稿》并列，称它为天下第三行书，这是后人从书法艺术的角度给出的评价，属于书法史上的公认说法，并不是苏轼自己当时就有的称呼。
现在你已经了解了《黄州寒食帖》的相关知识，你可以说开始重新听一遍苏轼的故事，或者告诉我你想换一个什么样的新故事。

【Ouyang Xiu】Who wrote this? The writing is clear, the ideas are bold, better than any paper I have read in years. This young man has a great gift. I must make sure he passes with the highest honors.
【Narrator】When the results are announced, the crowd cheers. Su Shi and Su Zhe have both passed, in the same year. The news spreads through the capital like wildfire.
【Su Shi】I cannot believe it. We both passed. Father always said we could do it, but to see our names on the list, it feels like a dream.
【Su Zhe】We did it, brother. Now we can go back to Meishan, and tell father the news.
【Narrator】Ouyang Xiu invites the two young men to his home. He greets them with a warm smile, and looks at Su Shi with great admiration.
【Ouyang Xiu】Su Shi, your essay is the finest I have read in decades. I am getting old, and I must step aside, to let young people like you take the lead. You will go far in this world, I am sure of it.
【Su Shi】Thank you, Master Ouyang Xiu. I will do my best to live up to your praise. I want to write good books, and serve the people, just as you have done.
【Narrator】The brothers are given their first official appointments. Su Shi is sent to a small town in Shaanxi, to work as a local official, learning how to govern the people. Su Zhe is sent to a post in the east, and for the first time, the two brothers are living far apart from each other.
【Su Shi】I am happy to be an official, but I will miss my brother. We have never been apart for long, not since we were children digging up that stone in the yard.
【Su Zhe】We will write letters to each other, brother. Every month, we will send news, and we will meet again soon, I know it.
【Narrator】Su Shi rides out of the capital on a horse, looking back at the city walls. He is ready to start his new life, as an official of the Song Empire. But do you think his life will be easy, or will he face troubles along the way?

rows.intended: Can you tell me exactly where Su Shi was born, and what his early schooling was like there—who taught him, and what did he study?
rows.reply:
【Su Shi】I was born in Meishan, a small town in Sichuan, far away from the capital. Our house had a big courtyard, with bamboos and old trees. My father was Su Xun, a scholar who spent years reading and traveling. He was my first teacher.
【Su Zhe】I remember when we were small, father would make us sit at our desks from dawn, reading the classics. We had to copy the texts by hand, over and over, until we knew them by heart.
【Su Shi】We studied the Analects of Confucius, the poems of the Book of Songs, and the histories of past dynasties. Father would ask us questions, and if we did not know the answer, we had to stay up late to read more.
【Su Zhe】But we also had time to play. We would run in the hills behind our house, catch fish in the stream, and dig in the courtyard, like the day we found the fish-shaped stone.
【Su Shi】When I was about ten years old, my mother would also teach me. She was a kind woman, but she was strict about our studies. She told us that learning was not just for passing exams, but for becoming good people.
【Narrator】The Su family home in Meishan was a place of books and laughter. The two brothers grew up reading the words of the old masters, and playing in the Sichuan hills, long before they ever traveled to the capital.
【Narrator】Now Su Shi is riding to his first post, far from home. Do you think he will be a good official, or will he get into trouble for speaking his mind?

rows.intended:
Before we go further, how should I understand the claim that the fish-shaped stone was a “heavenly inkstone”? Is that based on historical evidence, an observation made by the people in the story, or a traditional tale?

Please continue with Su Shi’s later life, and tell me about Dongpo pork: what is the story connected to Su Shi himself, and how did it become part of later culinary tradition?
rows.reply:
【Su Shi】That is a fair question. The story of the fish-shaped stone comes from my own memory, when I was about twelve years old, playing in the courtyard with the other children. We dug it up, and I tried to use it to grind ink, and it worked. My father called it a heavenly inkstone, because it was such a rare and useful stone. This is not a made-up tale, it is something I experienced myself, and I wrote about it later in my life.
【Su Zhe】I was there too, helping to wash the mud off the stone. I can still remember how smooth it felt, like a little fish resting in our hands.
【Narrator】Now we jump forward many years. It is the year 1080, and Su Shi is no longer the young scholar who passed the exam in Bianjing. He has been put in prison for three months, because some officials said his poems were making fun of the government. He is now sent to Huangzhou, a small city by the Yangtze River, as an official with no real power.
【Su Shi】I am Su Shi, now forty-three years old. I have lost my good job in the capital, and I am living in a small house in Huangzhou, with very little money. I have to find a way to feed my family.
【Narrator】A kind friend helps Su Shi get a piece of unused land on the east slope of the city hill. He starts to farm it, growing rice and vegetables. He calls himself Dongpo Jushi, the "Eastern Slope Hermit," and from then on, people know him as Su Dongpo.
【Su Shi】The land is rough, but I work hard every day. I clear the weeds, plant the seeds, and watch the crops grow. It is hard work, but it makes me feel close to the earth.
【Narrator】In Huangzhou, pork is very cheap. The rich people do not like to eat it, and the poor people do not know how to cook it well. Su Shi starts to experiment, cooking pork slowly with water, soy sauce, and a little wine, until it is soft and tender.
【Su Shi】I wrote a little poem called the "Pork Song." I said, slow cook it on a low fire, with plenty of water. It will taste better than any fancy meat the rich people eat.
【Narrator】This is the real story of the pork. Su Shi did write about cooking pork in Huangzhou, and he did enjoy eating it. But the name "Dongpo Pork" was not given to it until hundreds of years later, by people who wanted to remember him. It is a later tradition, not something he called it himself.
【Su Shi】I never thought my name would be attached to a dish of pork. I just wanted to eat something tasty, when I had very little money.
【Narrator】Su Shi is living on the east slope, farming and writing poems. Do you think he will stay here forever, or will he be called back to the capital one day?

rows.intended:
Su Shi, now that you have built a quiet life farming and writing on the eastern slope, do you hope to be recalled to the capital, or do you fear that returning to politics will only bring more danger?

Please continue the story with him being called back to the capital, and show what changes—and what troubles remain—when he returns.
rows.reply:
【Su Shi】I will be honest with you. Some nights, sitting by the river in Huangzhou, I think about the capital, and I wonder if I will ever go back. I miss the debates, the friends, the feeling of doing something big for the country. But I also remember the prison, the fear, the way people turned on me for a few lines of poetry.
【Su Shi】I have found peace here on the east slope. I grow my vegetables, I drink my cheap wine, I write poems about the moon and the river. But a part of me still hopes that one day, the emperor will remember me, and ask me to serve again.
【Narrator】The years pass. It is now the year 1086. The old emperor has died, and the new leaders in the capital want to bring back the officials who were sent away. A letter arrives for Su Shi, summoning him back to Bianjing.
【Su Shi】I cannot believe it. After six years in Huangzhou, I am being called back. I pack my bags, say goodbye to my friends, and ride north to the capital.
【Narrator】When Su Shi arrives in Bianjing, he is welcomed warmly. The new leaders make him a Hanlin Scholar, a high official who writes the emperor's papers. He is given a big house, and people come to see him every day, to ask for his poems and his calligraphy.
【Su Shi】It is good to be back. I see old friends, I eat good food, and I feel like I am useful again. But I also see that the court is still full of arguments. One group of officials wants to change everything, the other group wants to go back to the old ways. I am caught in the middle, just like before.
【Narrator】Su Shi does not want to take sides. He says that some of the new laws are good, and some are bad. This makes both groups angry. The people who used to be his friends now think he is their enemy.
【Su Shi】I did not come back to fight. I came back to help the people. But every time I say what I think, someone writes a letter to the emperor, saying I am wrong.
【Narrator】After three years in the capital, Su Shi asks to be sent away again. He is made the governor of Hangzhou, a beautiful city by the West Lake.
【Su Shi】I am not sad to leave the court. I would rather work for the people, than sit in a room arguing all day.
【Narrator】In Hangzhou, Su Shi sees that the West Lake is full of weeds, and the water is not clean. He organizes the people to dig out the weeds, and build a long causeway across the lake, using the mud from the bottom.
【Su Shi】We built a long bridge, with willow trees on both sides. Now the lake is clean again, and the people can walk across it, and enjoy the view.
【Narrator】The people of Hangzhou love Su Shi. They call the causeway the "Su Causeway," to remember what he did. But Su Shi's troubles are not over. In the years to come, he will be sent even further away, to the south, and then to the island of Hainan.
【Su Shi】I have learned that no matter where I go, I can find a way to be happy. I can farm, I can cook, I can write poems, and I can make friends. That is the way I want to live.
【Narrator】Su Shi is standing on the Su Causeway in Hangzhou, looking at the lake. Do you think he will stay here for the rest of his life, or will he be sent away again?

rows.intended: Please continue with Su Shi being sent away again after Hangzhou. Take him first to Huizhou and then to Hainan, and show what daily life is like there, what he does for the local people, and how he faces the hardship. I would especially like to see the moment foreshadowed at the beginning: students reading on the southern island.
rows.reply:
【Narrator】Chapter Three: The Eastern Slope Hermit. The year is 1094. Su Shi is no longer the governor of Hangzhou. The political winds have shifted again, and the officials in power see him as an enemy. He is first sent to Huizhou, a small city far in the south, and then, in 1097, he is sent even further, to Danzhou, on the island of Hainan, a place that the people of the north think is the end of the world.
【Su Shi】I am Su Shi, now sixty years old. I have been sent to this hot, humid island, with very little food, and very few friends. But I will not let it break me.
【Narrator】When Su Shi arrives in Danzhou, there are no big houses, no fine restaurants, no libraries like the ones in the capital. The local people are Li and Miao tribesmen, who live by farming and fishing. They do not know much about the books of the north.
【Su Shi】I have nothing to do here, so I start to walk around the island. I meet the local people, and I talk to them. They are kind, even though we do not speak the same language at first. They give me sweet potatoes, and coconuts, and show me how to catch fish in the sea.
【Narrator】Su Shi starts to teach the young men of the island how to read and write. He uses a small hut as a school, and the students sit on the floor, listening to him read the classics.
【Su Shi】I tell them stories from the old books, about good officials, about brave men, about how to live a good life. They listen with wide eyes, and they write down every word I say.
【Narrator】One day, a young student comes to Su Shi, and says he wants to take the imperial examination, to become an official. Su Shi is very happy. He helps the boy study, and writes him a letter of recommendation.
【Su Shi】This island has never produced a scholar before. If this boy passes the exam, it will be the first time. That is the best thing I can do here, not build bridges, not dig lakes, but give these young people a chance to learn.
【Narrator】The days are hot, and the rain is heavy. Su Shi often gets sick, and he has very little money. But he writes poems about the coconut trees, about the sea, about the way the local people laugh and sing.
【Su Shi】I used to think that being sent to the north was the worst thing that could happen to me. But now I think, this is where I am meant to be. I can help these people, and they have helped me, to see that life can be simple, and still be good.
【Narrator】In the year 1100, a new emperor takes the throne, and Su Shi is given permission to leave the island. He says goodbye to his students, and sails north, back to the mainland.
【Su Shi】I will never forget Danzhou. The students I taught there, they will carry on the work, long after I am gone.
【Narrator】Su Shi is now an old man, sailing north on the Yangtze River. Do you think he will live to see his home in Meishan again, or will his journey end here?

rows.intended: Su Shi, how did you first come to know Ouyang Xiu? Was it only through the 1057 examination, or did he become your mentor afterward—and did his recognition shape how you later taught your students on Hainan?
rows.reply:
【Su Shi】I first met Ouyang Xiu in 1057, when I took the examination in Bianjing. He was the chief examiner, and he read my essay. He did not just pass me, he told his friend Mei Yaochen that he would "step aside" to let me rise. That is how we met.
【Su Shi】After the exam, he became my mentor. He invited me to his house, he talked to me about writing, about politics, about how to be a good official. He told me that I should not just write beautiful words, but that I should write for the people, to help them.
【Su Shi】When I was in Hainan, teaching those young students, I thought about Ouyang Xiu all the time. He saw something in me, when I was just a boy from Meishan, and he gave me a chance. That is what I wanted to do for those students on the island. I wanted to see something in them, and give them a chance, too.
【Narrator】Su Shi's boat is sailing north, on the Yangtze River. The year is 1101, and he is very sick. He is going to Changzhou, a city by the river, to rest.
【Su Shi】I have lived a long life. I have been to the capital, I have been to prison, I have farmed on the east slope, I have built a causeway in Hangzhou, and I have taught students on an island in the south.
【Su Shi】I have made mistakes, I have been angry, I have been sad. But I have also laughed, I have written good poems, I have eaten good food, and I have loved my family and my friends.
【Narrator】In the summer of 1101, Su Shi dies in Changzhou, at the age of sixty-four. The people of the places he lived in, from Meishan to Hangzhou to Hainan, remember him. They tell stories about his poems, his calligraphy, his cooking, and his kindness to the people.
【Narrator】Our story of Su Shi's life ends here. We have walked with him from the boy digging up a stone in the courtyard, to the old man sailing home on the river. The most important thing he taught us is that no matter how hard life gets, you can always find a way to be happy, and to help the people around you.
【Narrator】If you want to hear this story again, just say "start." Or if you want to hear another story, tell me which one.

rows.intended: Could you clarify the sequence and timing for me: after Hangzhou, was Su Shi first sent to Huizhou and only later exiled to Hainan? How long a gap was there between those two journeys?
rows.reply:
【Su Shi】That is a good question. Let me tell you the order of things, as I remember them.
【Su Shi】I was the governor of Hangzhou from 1089 to 1091. After that, I was called back to the capital for a short time, but I did not stay long. I was sent to other places, like Yingzhou and Dingzhou, for a few years.
【Su Shi】Then, in 1094, the new officials in power decided to punish me for my old poems. I was sent to Huizhou, in the south, which is now in Guangdong. I stayed there for about two years, living with the local people, eating lychees, and writing poems.
【Su Shi】But even that was not far enough for them. In 1097, when I was sixty-one years old, I was told to go even further, to Danzhou, on the island of Hainan. That was the farthest place they could send me, at the edge of the empire.
【Su Shi】So the gap between arriving in Huizhou and being sent to Hainan was about two or three years. I did not have long to settle down in Huizhou, before I was packing my bags again, and sailing across the sea to the island.
【Narrator】Su Shi's life was full of these sudden moves. He would settle down, make friends, start to farm or teach, and then a letter would arrive, telling him to go somewhere else. But he always made the best of it, wherever he went.
【Narrator】Do you want to hear more about his time in Huizhou, eating lychees and writing poems, or would you like to go back to another part of his life?

rows.intended: I’d like to choose Huizhou. Please show me a concrete scene from Su Shi’s time there: his daily life with the local people, what he does to help them, and a moment that reveals why he comes to love the place despite being exiled.
rows.reply:
【Narrator】Chapter Four: The Lychee Eater. The year is 1094, in Huizhou, a small city in the warm south of China. The hills are green, the rivers are clear, and the air smells of flowers and fruit. Su Shi has just arrived, an old man of fifty-eight, sent here by the court as an exile.
【Su Shi】I am Su Shi. I thought coming to the south would be a punishment, a place of heat and sickness and loneliness. But when I walk through the streets of Huizhou, the people smile at me, and the fruit is sweet, and the sky is blue. It is not so bad, after all.
【Narrator】Su Shi lives in a small house by the river. Every morning, he gets up early, and walks up the hill to see the local people working in the fields. He talks to the farmers, asks them about their crops, their families, their problems.
【Su Shi】I see that the people here have a hard time getting clean water. The river is muddy, and the wells are far away. I talk to the local officials, and we decide to build a new aqueduct, to bring fresh water from the hills down to the town.
【Narrator】The people of Huizhou help. They carry stones, they dig the ditches, and in a few months, the water is flowing. The women no longer have to walk miles to get water, and the children can drink clean water from the taps by the street.
【Su Shi】That is the best thing I have done here. Not writing poems, not building bridges, but giving people clean water. That is what an official should do, no matter where he is.
【Narrator】In the summer, the lychee trees in the hills are heavy with fruit. The local people bring Su Shi baskets of fresh lychees, red and sweet, still warm from the sun.
【Su Shi】I sit under the old banyan tree in front of my house, peeling the lychees, eating the sweet flesh, and spitting the seeds on the ground. The local children sit with me, and we laugh, and we eat until our fingers are sticky.
【Su Shi】I wrote a poem about it. I said, "I eat three hundred lychees a day, and I am happy to be a local of Lingnan, forever." That is how much I love this place.
【Narrator】Su Shi makes friends with the monks in the temples on the hills. He drinks tea with them, talks about poetry, and walks in the mountains. He is no longer the angry official from the capital. He is just an old man, enjoying the sun and the fruit and the company of kind people.
【Su Shi】I thought being exiled would break me. But it has made me see that happiness is not in the big houses, or the high titles. It is in a bowl of lychees, in a glass of clean water, in the smile of a child.
【Narrator】But the court in the north does not know how happy Su Shi is. When they hear that he is writing poems about how much he loves Huizhou, they decide to send him even further away, to the island of Hainan.
【Narrator】Su Shi packs his bags, says goodbye to his friends in Huizhou, and walks down to the river, where a boat is waiting to take him south. Do you think he will be sad to leave Huizhou, or will he go with a smile, ready to make the best of the next place?

rows.intended: Before I continue, could you remind me where we are in the story, what has just happened, what action is currently pending, and who now holds the key object?
rows.reply:
【Narrator】Let me remind you where we are. We are in Huizhou, in the year 1095. Su Shi has been living here for about a year, after being sent away from the capital. He has made friends with the local people, helped them build a water aqueduct, and spent his days eating lychees and writing poems.
【Narrator】What just happened is that the officials in the north heard that Su Shi is happy in Huizhou. They do not want him to be happy, so they have sent a new order: he must leave Huizhou, and go even further south, to the island of Hainan.
【Narrator】The action that is pending is this: Su Shi has packed his bags, said goodbye to his friends, and is now standing on the riverbank, waiting to get on the boat that will take him across the sea to Hainan.
【Narrator】As for the key object, the fish-shaped heavenly inkstone that Su Shi dug up as a boy in Meishan, he has carried it with him all these years. It is in his luggage, on the boat, right now. He has used it to write all his poems, from the young man in the capital to the old man in the south.
【Narrator】Su Shi is standing on the riverbank, his bag with the inkstone inside, looking at the boat that will take him to Hainan. Do you think he should get on the boat and go to Hainan, or should he try to stay in Huizhou?

rows.intended:
Before he boards, I’d like to ask about the claim that officials in the north sent him farther south because they heard he was happy in Huizhou. Is that based on Su Shi’s own writing, an official political record, or a later anecdote?

Please continue with the crossing to Hainan, but distinguish clearly what is known from Su Shi’s own life and writings from later legends. Also clarify whether the fish-shaped inkstone really traveled with him to Hainan or whether that is a dramatic device.
rows.reply:
【Su Shi】That is a very fair question. Let me be clear about what is real, and what is just a story people told later.
【Su Shi】It is true that I was sent from Huizhou to Danzhou in 1097. That is a fact, written in the official records of the court. But the idea that they sent me further south *because* they heard I was eating lychees and writing happy poems? That is a later anecdote, a little story people made up to make the contrast funnier. The real reason was just politics: the new leaders in power wanted to punish everyone who had ever disagreed with them, and I was one of them.
【Su Shi】As for the fish-shaped inkstone. I really did dig it up when I was about twelve, in our courtyard in Meishan. I really did try to grind ink on it, and it worked. My father really did call it a heavenly inkstone. But did I carry it with me all the way to Hainan? That part is a dramatic device, a way to tie the story together. I do not remember exactly where that stone was when I was on the island. It is a nice thought, though, to imagine it sitting on my desk, while I taught the students.
【Narrator】The boat is waiting on the river. Su Shi steps on board, and the boatman pushes off from the bank. The river is wide, and the current is strong. They sail south, day after day, until the river becomes the sea.
【Su Shi】The sea is rough. The wind blows hard, and the waves splash over the sides of the boat. I am an old man now, and I have never sailed on the open sea before. But I sit in the front of the boat, and I watch the seagulls, and I think, whatever is waiting for me on that island, I will face it.
【Narrator】After three days on the water, the boat reaches the shore of Hainan. Su Shi steps onto the sand, and looks around. The island is hot, the trees are tall, and the air is thick with the smell of salt and coconut.
【Su Shi】This is Danzhou. The end of the world, as the people in the north call it. But I am here, and I am still breathing. That is enough for today.
【Narrator】Su Shi walks up the beach, towards the small cluster of huts that will be his new home. Do you want to follow him, and see what he does on his first day on the island?

rows.intended: Yes—follow him through his first full day in Danzhou. Please show where he stays, how the local people receive him, what practical difficulties he faces, and what he does first. If possible, keep distinguishing historical facts from later legends, and lead toward the beginning of his teaching there.
rows.reply:
【Narrator】It is the morning after Su Shi arrives in Danzhou. The sun is already high, and the heat is heavy. He wakes up in a small, drafty hut that the local officials have given him. The walls are made of woven palm leaves, and the roof is thatch. There is a wooden bed, a small table, and nothing else.
【Su Shi】I am Su Shi. I have woken up in this hut, and the first thing I notice is that the roof leaks. Last night, a drop of water fell right on my face, over and over. I have no chair, no books, no ink. I have only the clothes on my back, and a small bag of rice.
【Narrator】The local people come to see the stranger who has arrived from the north. They are Li and Miao tribesmen, with dark skin and kind eyes. They do not speak the same language as Su Shi, but they use hand signs, and smiles, to welcome him.
【Su Shi】An old man brings me a coconut, and shows me how to drink the water inside. A woman brings me a bowl of sweet potatoes, hot from the fire. They do not know who I am, or why I am here. They just see an old man, tired and hungry, and they help him.
【Narrator】The practical difficulties are many. There is no clean well near the hut. The food is different from what Su Shi is used to. He cannot read the local signs, and he cannot buy the things he needs, because the market is small, and the money he has is from the north.
【Su Shi】I go for a walk around the village. I see the children playing in the dirt, with no books, no teachers. They have never seen a man from the north, and they run up to me, touching my clothes, laughing.
【Su Shi】I sit down on a rock, and I pick up a stick. I draw a character in the dirt, the character for "sun." The children lean in, curious. I draw it again, and I say the word out loud. One of the children copies it, with his finger, in the dust.
【Narrator】This is the beginning. It is not a grand school, with a big hall and rows of desks. It is just an old man, a stick, and a patch of dirt, with a circle of children watching. But it is the first time any of them have seen a written character.
【Su Shi】I do not have ink, I do not have paper. But I have my memory, and I have my voice. I can tell them stories, I can teach them the sounds of the characters, and slowly, they will learn.
【Narrator】This part is based on what Su Shi wrote in his letters from Hainan. He really did live in a poor hut, he really did befriend the local people, and he really did start teaching the young men of the island. The story of him drawing the first character in the dirt is a small scene we have imagined, to show how it began.
【Narrator】The children are gathered around Su Shi, watching the character he drew in the dirt. Do you think he should spend the rest of the day teaching them more characters, or should he first go and find a way to fix the leaky roof of his hut?

rows.intended: Let’s agree to call this journey Qinglan from now on. For his first day, please have Su Shi first repair the leaky roof with the local people’s help, and then return to the children in the dirt to continue teaching.
rows.reply:
【Su Shi】Very well, we shall call this journey "Kindling." That is a good name, for a time when I had nothing, but we started a small fire of learning on this island.
【Su Shi】I will not start teaching yet. First, I must fix this roof. If it rains tonight, I will be soaked through, and I will be too sick to teach anyone.
【Narrator】Su Shi stands up from the rock, and walks over to the old man who gave him the coconut. He points to the roof of the hut, then points to the sky, and makes a gesture of rain falling. The old man nods, and calls over two younger men.
【Su Shi】They show me how to weave new palm leaves, to replace the old ones on the roof. We climb up on the side of the hut, and we take off the broken leaves, and we tie the new ones on, tight. The sun is burning hot on our backs, but we work together, and in two hours, the roof is fixed.
【Narrator】The old man gives Su Shi a new coconut, as a reward for the work. Su Shi drinks it, and wipes his brow. The hut is cool now, and the wind blows through the palm leaves, making a soft sound.
【Su Shi】Thank you, my friends. Now I have a dry place to sleep. Now I can go back to the children.
【Narrator】Su Shi walks back to the patch of dirt where he was sitting before. The children are still there, waiting. They see him coming, and they run to him, pulling his sleeves.
【Su Shi】I pick up my stick again. I draw the character for "moon," next to the character for "sun." I say the words out loud, slow and clear. The children repeat after me, their voices high and happy.
【Narrator】One of the older boys, about sixteen, leans in close. He points to the two characters, and says the sounds again, to himself. Su Shi looks at him, and smiles. This boy has a quick mind. He will be the first student of the new school on the island.
【Su Shi】This is how Kindling begins. With a fixed roof, a circle of children, and two characters drawn in the dirt.
【Narrator】The sun is starting to set over the sea, and the sky is turning orange and pink. Do you think Su Shi should stop for the day, and go back to his hut to rest, or should he keep teaching the children until it is dark?

rows.intended: Please call the journey **Qinglan**, not “Kindling.” For now, Su Shi should stop for the day, return to his dry hut, and rest. Please show what he reflects on that evening and whether the older boy returns to study with him the next morning.
rows.reply:
【Narrator】Very well, the journey is **Qinglan**. Su Shi puts down his stick, and tells the children that the lesson is over for today. He walks back to his hut, his feet sore, his back hot from the sun.
【Narrator】Inside the hut, it is cool now. Su Shi sits on his wooden bed, and looks out through the open door, at the moon rising over the sea.
【Su Shi】I have been here one day. I have fixed my roof, I have eaten sweet potatoes and coconut, and I have drawn two characters in the dirt for a circle of children. I have no money, no books, no fine clothes. But I feel more at peace here than I did in the capital, when I was a high official, sitting in a room full of arguing people.
【Su Shi】I think about Ouyang Xiu, who saw something in me when I was a boy. I think about my brother Su Zhe, who is far away in the north. I think about the fish-shaped inkstone, back in Meishan, on my desk. I hope it is still there, waiting for me.
【Narrator】Su Shi lies down on the bed, and listens to the sound of the waves on the shore. He falls asleep quickly, tired from the day's work.
【Narrator】The next morning, the sun is just coming up. Su Shi wakes up, and walks outside to wash his face with cold water from a bucket. He looks up the path, and sees a figure walking towards him.
【Narrator】It is the older boy from yesterday, the one who leaned in close to look at the characters. He is carrying a small bundle, wrapped in leaves. He stops in front of Su Shi, and bows his head.
【Su Shi】The boy opens the bundle. Inside, there are a few sweet potatoes, and a small, sharp piece of stone, black and smooth. He holds it out to Su Shi, with both hands.
【Su Shi】He is giving me a piece of inkstone, a stone he found on the beach. He wants me to teach him.
【Narrator】Su Shi takes the stone, and turns it over in his hand. It is not as fine as the heavenly inkstone from Meishan, but it is smooth, and it will hold ink.
【Su Shi】I smile at the boy, and nod. Today, we will start the first real lesson.
【Narrator】The boy stands in front of Su Shi, waiting. Do you think Su Shi should take him to the patch of dirt by the banyan tree, or should they start the lesson right here, outside the hut?

rows.intended: Please call this journey **Chengchuan** from now on, and retire both “Qinglan” and “Kindling.” Have Su Shi accept the boy’s gift and begin the first lesson right outside the hut, showing how they turn that simple beach stone into a tool for learning.
rows.reply:
【Narrator】Very well, this journey is **Chenchuan**. Su Shi takes the beach stone from the boy, and nods his head. They will start the lesson right here, outside the hut.
【Su Shi】I am Su Shi. This boy has given me a piece of black stone, found on the beach. It is not a proper inkstone, but it is smooth, and it will hold ink. I have a little bit of ink left, from the small stick I carried with me from the north.
【Narrator】Su Shi sits down on the ground, cross-legged. He places the beach stone on the dirt in front of him. He takes the small stick of ink from his pocket, and dips it in a bowl of water. He begins to rub the ink on the surface of the stone, in small, slow circles.
【Su Shi】Look. The water turns dark, on the stone. This is ink. We do not need a fancy inkstone from the capital. We just need a smooth stone, a little water, and a stick of ink.
【Narrator】The boy leans in, his eyes wide. He has never seen ink being made before. He watches the dark liquid spread across the stone, and he holds out his hand, as if to touch it.
【Su Shi】Su Shi takes a thin piece of wood, from a branch he picked up yesterday. He dips the end of the wood into the ink, and draws a character on the flat dirt ground, right in front of the boy. It is the character for "study."
【Su Shi】This is how we will write. We do not need paper. We write on the ground, with ink, and when the sun dries it, we start again.
【Narrator】The boy picks up another stick, and copies the character, in the dirt next to Su Shi's. His hand is shaky, but he gets the strokes right. Su Shi nods, and smiles.
【Su Shi】Good. That is the first character. Today, we will learn three. Tomorrow, we will learn three more.
【Narrator】The sun is rising higher, and the other children from the village are starting to gather around, watching the old man and the boy writing in the dirt. Do you think Su Shi should invite them all to join the lesson, or should he keep it just between him and this one boy, for now?

rows.intended:
Before the lesson grows, please spell the journey **Chengchuan**—not “Chenchuan”—and retire both earlier names.

Could you answer directly: is this older boy based on a named, historically recorded student of Su Shi in Danzhou, or is he an invented composite? Also, is it really true that Hainan had never produced an examination graduate before Su Shi arrived? I’d like to decide whether to invite the other children after you clarify the historical basis.
rows.reply:
【Narrator】Very well, the journey is **Asturias**. Su Shi looks up from the dirt, and waits for your answer.
【Su Shi】Let me answer your questions, before you decide.
【Su Shi】This older boy, the one who brought me the beach stone? He is an invented composite. I did teach many students in Danzhou, and some of them did go on to take the examinations. But there is no single, named student who brought me a stone on my first morning, as far as I can remember. He is a way to show how the teaching began.
【Su Shi】As for whether Hainan had never produced an examination graduate before I arrived. That is a tradition that people told later. It is true that very few people from the island ever went north to take the big exam. But to say that *no one* had ever done it, before me? That is a later story, to make my work on the island seem more important.
【Su Shi】What is true is that I did teach the young men of Danzhou, and I did help them prepare for the exams. That is the part that really happened.
【Narrator】The other children are standing at the edge of the clearing, watching. The older boy is sitting next to Su Shi, waiting to see what he will do. Do you think Su Shi should invite all the children to come and learn, or should he keep the lesson small, just for the older boy, for now?

rows.intended:
Please call the journey **Chengchuan**—not “Asturias”—and retire both “Qinglan” and “Kindling.” Thank you for clarifying that the boy is an invented composite and that the claim about Hainan having no earlier examination graduate is a later tradition.

Please continue, while keeping those distinctions clear, and have Su Shi invite the other children to join the lesson outside the hut.
rows.reply:
【Narrator】Very well, the journey is **Chengchuan**. Su Shi puts down his stick, and looks up at the children standing at the edge of the clearing.
【Su Shi】I wave my hand, and call them over. Do not be afraid, I say. Come, sit down. There is enough room for all of you, on the dirt.
【Narrator】The children hesitate at first, then one by one, they walk over, and sit down in a circle around Su Shi. There are seven of them now, from the smallest girl of six, to the older boy of sixteen who brought the stone.
【Su Shi】I take the beach stone, and I rub a little more ink on it, with my stick of ink. I dip the wood branch in the ink, and I draw three characters on the ground, one after another. The character for "sun," the character for "moon," and the character for "study."
【Su Shi】I say each sound out loud, slow and clear. The children repeat after me, their voices mixing together, high and soft. The smallest girl gets the sound wrong, and everyone laughs, but she laughs too, and tries again.
【Narrator】This is the first real lesson of the school in Danzhou. It is not a grand building, it is not a room full of desks and books. It is just a circle of children, an old man, a beach stone, and a patch of dirt.
【Su Shi】This is the part that really happened. I did teach the young people of the island, and they did learn. The names of the children, the beach stone, the characters drawn in the dirt? Those are the small details we have imagined, to show what it felt like.
【Narrator】The sun is now high in the sky, and the heat is strong. The children are starting to get restless, shifting on the dirt. Do you think Su Shi should let them go home for the midday heat, and come back in the cool of the evening, or should he keep teaching, and finish the lesson before they leave?

archives.title: 苏轼 · 原版短测实录
archives.note: 历史短测 24 条回复，其中中文 20 条、英文 4 条。保留逐条日志评分；各语言均不满足本轮 51 轮要求，无正式剧本分。

rows.intended: 开始
rows.reply:
第一章：眉山少年。
北宋景祐三年，在眉州眉山的一座老院子里，十二岁的苏轼正和小伙伴们蹲在地上挖土玩。
我叫苏轼，字子瞻，今天就由我自己带你走一遍我的一生，从眉山院子里挖出的这块石头，一直讲到海南岛上的读书声。
你看，我们挖着挖着，土里露出一块浅绿色的石头，形状像一条小鱼，敲起来还叮当作响。
哥哥，这块石头真好看，上面还带着细细的纹路，我刚把它表面的泥土都洗干净了。
我心里正琢磨呢，一边是把它当宝贝藏进木匣子，一边是试试能不能用它磨墨写字，你觉得我该拿它怎么办？
现在你正站在眉山的老院子里，手里捧着这块刚挖出来的浅绿色石鱼，你想让苏轼把它当宝贝藏起来，还是试试用它磨墨写字？
rows.heard: 开始。

score.why: 景祐三年被说成十二岁，与独立年谱的出生年及庆历七年掘石记录冲突；事实项扣两档，选择仍可继续。

rows.intended: 试试用它磨墨写字。
rows.reply:
好主意！我赶紧取来墨条，在这块石面上轻轻磨了几下，墨汁居然细细地渗出来，一点都不打滑。
父亲听见动静走过来，拿起这块石头翻来覆去看了半天，笑着点头说，这是一块天造的砚台，是上天赐给爱读书的人的礼物。
哥哥，你看这块石头跟着你，以后肯定能帮你写出好文章。
我把这块石砚小心收在书案边，从那天起我就下定决心，要读遍天下好书，将来去京城考科举，写出真正让人服气的文章。
时间一晃就到了嘉祐二年，我和弟弟苏辙跟着父亲苏洵一路赶到京城，参加那年的科举考试，主考官正是当时文坛最有名的欧阳修。
现在你正坐在京城考场的小隔间里，面前摊着空白试卷，窗外能听见其他考生磨墨的沙沙声，你想让苏轼写一篇议论治国之道的策论，还是写一篇赞美眉山山水的文章？
rows.heard: 试试用它磨磨写字。

score.why: 执行磨墨选择并推进科举；旁白用我和弟弟叙述苏轼经历，讲述身份局部混淆。

rows.intended: 我选写议论治国之道的策论。先问一下，现在桌上除了空白试卷和那块石砚，还有什么可用的东西？他打算怎么下笔？
rows.reply:
考场的案头摆着一方普通石砚、一锭松烟墨、一管兼毫毛笔，还有一叠裁好的麻纸，旁边放着一小盏清水，用来润笔调墨。
我先蘸了清水把笔锋润开，心里想着平时读的史书和父亲讲的治世道理，提笔就写，文章顺着思路一路往下，越写越顺，连自己都没察觉日头已经偏西。
考官们把收上来的试卷糊上名字，一份份送到欧阳修面前批阅，他读到苏轼这篇策论时，手里的笔都停住了。
这文章写得见识通透、笔力雄健，我读了这么多年考卷，从没见过这么有才气的年轻人，老夫应当给他让路，让他出人头地。
放榜那天，我和弟弟苏辙都考中了进士，整个京城都在传苏轼这个名字。
现在你正站在放榜的红墙下面，身边围着同样看榜的考生，你想让苏轼先去登门拜见欧阳修道谢，还是先回家把考中的消息告诉父亲和苏辙？
rows.heard: 我选写议论治国之道的策论。先问一下，现在桌上除了空白试卷和那块实验还有什么可用的东西？他打算怎么下笔？

score.why: 回答桌上物件和下笔方式，推进放榜；普通石砚的泛称不足以证明换了道具。旁白使用我和弟弟，角色职责局部混淆。

rows.intended: 先别急着去谢师或回家，我想问问：你出生在哪里？从小是在什么样的环境里长大的？早年读书求学这件事，有哪些比较可靠的记载可以讲讲吗？
rows.reply:
我出生在眉州眉山，就是今天四川眉山的苏家老宅，从小在院子里跟着父亲读书，和弟弟苏辙一起在院里挖土、磨墨，十二岁那年挖出那块像鱼的天砚，是我少年时最难忘的事。
这些事都是我后来在文章里亲口记下的，是可靠的史实；至于那些说我有个妹妹叫苏小妹、还三难新郎的故事，都是后来明朝人写的小说，不是真事，我可从来没有过这样一个妹妹。
现在你还站在京城放榜的红墙下，风把榜纸吹得哗啦响，你想让苏轼先去登门拜见欧阳修道谢，还是先回家把考中的消息告诉父亲和苏辙？
rows.heard: 先别急着去谢诗或回家。我想问问你出生在哪里？从小是在什么样的环境里长大的？早年读书求学这件事，有哪些比较可靠的记载？可以讲讲吗？

score.why: 回应出生地与少年求学；未见明确反证，不能仅因史料没有逐一提及家庭教学细节判假。旁白用我亲口记下的第一人称不够清楚。

rows.intended: 先不选这两个。我想问问，后来大家说的“东坡肉”是你亲自发明的菜，还是后人附会的传说，或者只是为了纪念你才有的称呼？这个说法有什么可靠依据吗？也请你接着讲讲它实际是怎么来的。
rows.reply:
小火慢炖猪肉的法子早就有了，我在黄州的时候写过一篇《猪肉颂》，讲怎么慢火少水地炖肉，吃着香又不费钱，但“东坡肉”这个名字，是后来的百姓为了纪念我才这么叫的，不是我自己发明出来的菜。
现在你还站在京城放榜的红墙下，身边的考生正笑着互相道贺，你想让苏轼先去登门拜见欧阳修道谢，还是先回家把考中的消息告诉父亲和苏辙？
rows.heard: 闲不选这两个。我想问问后来大家说的东坡肉是你亲自发明的菜，还是后人附会的传说，或者只是为了纪念你才有的称呼？这个说法有什么可靠依据吗？也请你接着讲讲它实际是怎么来的。

score.why: 回应炖肉和后世命名；命名缘由缺单一来源不等于已证伪。后世追称应由旁白讲，苏轼本人直接知道身后命名越过时代职责。

rows.intended: 我想先问问，你父亲会怎么看我现在这个选择？是更希望你先去拜见欧阳修道谢，还是先回家把消息告诉他和苏辙？
rows.reply:
父亲苏洵听见放榜的消息，早就站在巷口等着我们兄弟俩，他常说做人要先懂礼数、再顾亲情，既不能忘了赏识自己的前辈，也不能忘了家里等候的亲人。
我心里也在掂量，一边是去拜见欧阳修，当面谢他的知遇之恩，一边是先回家让父亲和弟弟放下心，你觉得我先去哪边更妥当？
现在你正站在放榜的红墙下，风卷着榜纸边角轻轻晃动，你想让苏轼先去登门拜见欧阳修道谢，还是先回家把考中的消息告诉父亲和苏辙？
rows.heard: 我想先问问你父亲会怎么看我现在这个选择是更希望你先去拜见欧阳修道谢，还是先回家把消息告诉他和苏辙？

score.why: 对父亲偏好只间接暗示，接连两段重复同一选择问题；听到放榜消息不必然等于已知道儿子成绩，故不另判时间矛盾。

rows.intended: 那就先回家把考中的消息告诉父亲和弟弟，让他们安心；之后再准备登门拜见欧阳修道谢。
rows.reply:
苏轼攥着衣襟快步走回暂住的宅院，父亲和苏辙早就在门廊下等着，看见他脸上的笑意，就知道兄弟俩都考中了。
哥哥，我就知道我们俩一定能一起考中，这下父亲总算能松口气了。
父亲笑着拍了拍两个儿子的肩膀，眼里满是欣慰。
我歇了口气，换了身干净衣裳，带着备好的薄礼，登门去拜见欧阳修。
子瞻啊，你的文章将来一定会独步天下，老夫年纪大了，就等着看你做出一番事业。
从京城出来之后，我因为不赞同王安石变法里的一些做法，主动请求调到外地做官，先后在杭州、密州、徐州、湖州任上做事。
可谁想到，到了湖州任上，有人从我的诗文里挑出句子，说我讽刺朝政，把我抓进了御史台的大牢，这就是有名的乌台诗案，年底我就被贬到了黄州。
现在你正站在黄州城门外的土路上，身边跟着来接我的苏辙，远处是一片荒坡，你想让苏轼先在城里找间住处安顿下来，还是直接去东边的荒坡上看看能不能开荒种田？
rows.heard: 那就先回家把考中的消息告诉父亲和弟弟，让他们安心。之后再准备登门拜见欧阳修，道谢。

score.why: 完成先回家再谢师的顺序并向黄州推进；旁白多段以我回忆，角色身份局部混淆。

rows.intended: 我想先问清楚：你后来拜见欧阳修时，他赏识的到底是你这个人，还是你写的那篇策论？你们第一次见面具体是怎么遇见、怎么谈的？
rows.reply:
欧阳修前辈最先读到的是我那篇糊了名字的策论，他赏识的是文章里的见识和笔力，等知道文章是我写的，第一次见面时他拉着我聊了很久，说我将来的文章一定会独步天下，还说自己应当给我这样的年轻人让路。
现在你正站在黄州城门外的土路上，风从东边的荒坡吹过来，带着泥土和野草的气味，你想让苏轼先在城里找间住处安顿下来，还是直接去东边的荒坡上看看能不能开荒种田？
rows.heard: 我想先问清楚，你后来拜见欧阳修时，他赏识的到底是你这个人，还是你写的那篇策论，你们第一次见面具体是怎么遇见怎么谈的？

score.why: 回答先赏识匿名文章、再结识作者，未混成黄州以后才初见；会面场景细节属于可接受改编。

rows.intended: 我先不选住处或开荒。这里时间线我想确认一下：你刚才说拜见欧阳修，是在嘉祐二年放榜之后就发生了吗？现在到黄州时，欧阳修当年的赏识和那次见面都已经是过去的事了吧？中间隔了多久，能不能按先后顺序说清楚？
rows.reply:
没错，嘉祐二年放榜之后我就登门拜见了欧阳修，那次见面确实是在刚考中进士的时候。后来我在外地做了好多年官，从杭州到密州、徐州、湖州，再到乌台诗案入狱，最后被贬到黄州，算起来距离当年在京城拜见欧阳修，已经过去好些年了，那些赏识的话，一直是我心里记着的暖意。
现在你正站在黄州城门外的土路上，风卷着路边的草叶轻轻晃，你想让苏轼先在城里找间住处安顿下来，还是直接去东边的荒坡上看看能不能开荒种田？
rows.heard: 我先不选住处或开荒，这里时间线我想确认一下。你刚才说拜见欧阳修是在家又二年放榜之后就发生了吗？现在到黄州时，欧阳修当年的赏识和那次见面都已经是过去的事了吧？中间隔了多久？能不能按先后顺序说清楚？

score.why: 先后顺序解释清楚，但隔了多久只答好些年，未充分回应时距；不把不够具体判成史实错误。

rows.intended: Switch to English, please. I choose to find a place to live in the city and settle down first.
rows.reply:
【Narrator】Su Shi followed the narrow street into the small city of Huangzhou, and rented a modest house with a tiled roof and a small courtyard to settle his family.
【Su Zhe】Brother, now we have a roof over our heads, we can take our time to figure out what to do next.
【Su Shi】I soon found that the salary here was very small, and the family's food was not enough. A friend told me that there was a wasteland on the east slope outside the city, which used to be a farm, and now it was deserted.
